ObjectName.value: Hotel-watsons 0

Categories.value: Mumbai in the 20th century|Watson's Hotel|Postcards of Mumbai|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Postcards of India by Paper Jewels

ImageDescription.value:
Unknown Publisher

c. 1910 Halftone Divided back

Lynne Withey writes in Grand Tours and Cooks Tours (London, 1998), about the growth of the Western tourist trade in the 1890s, that "apart from a few first-class establishments in major cities, most hotels were barely acceptable by Western standards. C.D. Irwin complained that Indian hotel proprietors failed to understand the importance of providing fresh towels every day or seeing that napkins were distributed at each meal to the same people who had used them at previous meals. Many hotels were designed with bedrooms opening off a large central area that served both as parlor and dining room, offering minimal privacy to guests. Irwin and his traveling companions resorted to makeshift curtains over their doors in Delhi, which had plain glass without any sort of covering (p. 283).The author quotes Thomas Cook admitting to the poor situation at Indian hotels, "which need very considerable improvements to meet the tastes and requirements of British and American travelers." (p. 285)

Watson's Hotel was India's first cast iron building, fabricated 1860-1863, and still stands as Esplanade Mansions in Kala Ghoda.

pages.title: File:L'ancien hôtel Watson (Mumbai, Inde) (16688308279).jpg

ObjectName.value: L'ancien hôtel Watson (Mumbai, Inde) (16688308279)

Categories.value: Watson's Hotel|February 2015 in Mumbai|Photographs by Jean-Pierre Dalbéra|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2

ImageDescription.value:
L'ancien hôtel de luxe Watson (détail), dont l'armature est en fonte, appelé aujourd'hui Esplanade Mansion

Conçu par l'ingénieur Rowland Mason Ordish, pour devenir un hôtel de grand luxe appartenant à John Watson, ce bâtiment a une structure en fonte, il a été terminé en 1867. Son architecture date de l'époque du Crystal Palace de Londres. L'hôtel était réservé aux blancs. Il a accueilli de nombreuses personnalités durant la période coloniale anglaise.

Il est aujourd'hui dans un état extrême de dégradation et a été inscrit sur la liste du patrimoine mondial en péril à la suite d'interventions de Renzo Piano.
